comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C6-C7 and C17-C21 regarding the core theoretical framework. Both evaluations rate these as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the theoretical derivation is valid but requires experimental validation, while peer reviewers explicitly affirm the model 'effectively illustrates' the proposed mechanism and is 'novel and well-implemented.'

Perfect agreement on claims C38-C41 regarding experimental consistency. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval appropriately notes these are post-hoc comparisons rather than direct tests, while peer reviewers accept the consistency with existing findings, acknowledging the model 'does align with empirical observations' though 'has not yet been compared directly to data.'

Perfect agreement on claims C50-C52 regarding clinical implications. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the connection is reasonable but speculative without direct testing, while peer reviewers accept these as testable predictions without challenging the cited associations between disorders and inhibitory dysfunction.

Perfect agreement on claims C59-C62 regarding synaptic plasticity mechanisms. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval cites experimental and theoretical work supporting biological plausibility, while peer reviewers confirm the simulations 'effectively illustrate that, with appropriate synaptic plasticity' the circuit functions as proposed.

Strong agreement on claims C25, C42-C45 regarding adaptive learning rates. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval identifies these as key functional predictions directly supported by Figure 7, while peer reviewers explicitly confirm 'the level of uncertainty automatically tunes the learning rate' and note the model 'yields a range of testable predictions.'

Agreement on claims C8, C22, C30 regarding SST learning of mean representations. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes this is a computational prediction requiring experimental validation, while peer reviewers explicitly state 'SSTs learn to represent the mean' and confirm 'the simulations shown demonstrate that...the authors' theory works very well.'

Divergence on claims C8, C22, C31 regarding PV variance encoding. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED noting the model shows PV firing rates become proportional to variance, though requiring validation. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 explicitly identifying the PV uncertainty encoding assumption as 'rather speculative' despite accepting it makes 'experimentally testable predictions.'

Agreement on claims C53-C58 regarding biological plausibility of model assumptions. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes these appropriately contextualize the model within neurophysiological knowledge, while peer reviewers confirm the framework is 'biologically plausible and matches some known biological data' with 'at least some biological support.'

Agreement on claims C23-C24, C35-C37 regarding dendritic nonlinearity and out-of-distribution detection. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the mechanism is based on established neurophysiological properties but requires experimental validation, while peer reviewers acknowledge the model 'yields testable predictions' and is 'biologically plausible' without specifically challenging these mechanisms.

Agreement on claims C1-C3, C10-C12 regarding theoretical foundations. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval identifies these as well-accepted theoretical foundations representing established knowledge, while peer reviewers confirm 'There is ample experimental evidence for prediction error responses in cortex' and validate the identified knowledge gap.

Agreement on claims C4-C5, C13-C16 regarding prior experimental findings and knowledge gaps. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes these accurately summarize prior work and establish motivation, while peer reviewers acknowledge 'a central prediction of the theory' addresses uncertainty modulation and confirm 'The impact of uncertainty on prediction errors in an understudied topic.'

Agreement on claims C27-C29 regarding circuit architecture. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes these are well-supported by experimental citations and establish the circuit basis, while peer reviewers confirm the framework is 'biologically plausible' with appropriate discussion of key assumptions.

Agreement on claim C49 regarding hierarchical processing extension. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN noting it lacks direct computational demonstration or extensive validation despite being conceptually consistent. Peer reviewers include this in a broader SUPPORTED evaluation but do not specifically address the hierarchical extension, suggesting implicit acceptance without detailed scrutiny.

Partial overlap on claim C23 regarding dendritic mechanisms. OpenEval groups C23 with C24, C35-C37 in a SUPPORTED evaluation of dendritic nonlinearity and error amplification. Peer reviewers include C23 with C8, C22, C30 in a SUPPORTED evaluation focused on SST mean learning, showing different grouping but consistent positive assessment.
